questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How charity shops raise money by selling people's old clothes
Paying a lot to look like you wear second-hand clothes
Why teenagers dress badly
The history of the Oxfam charity
questions.why: They discuss 'scumbro', which is about buying expensive designer brands that look like charity shop clothes.

questions.q: What does Rob say about charity shops?
options: He never goes into them
They have become far too expensive for most people
He finds bargains there and gives things too
They only sell old clothes
questions.why: Rob says they're a great place to pick up a bargain and he donates items to them too.

questions.q: What does Rob find strange about the scumbro style?
options: Expensive brands that look like charity shop clothes
It is only worn by women
It uses very bright colours
It was invented by a charity to help raise more money
questions.why: Rob says it's about buying expensive designer brands that look like they're from a charity shop. 'Very odd!'

questions.q: According to Amber Graafland, how did the trend spread?
options: Through charity shop adverts
Through school uniforms
Through a popular TV fashion show about second-hand clothes
Celebrities started it, then everyone copied
questions.why: She says trends like this are started by celebrities and then picked up by everybody.

questions.q: Where did the name 'scumbro' come from, according to Amber Graafland?
options: A song by Justin Bieber
An article in Vanity Fair
The Daily Mirror newspaper
A charity shop in Oxford
questions.why: She says 'I think the name came from a Vanity Fair article'.

questions.q: How does Amber Graafland describe the clothes?
options: Oversized and very expensive
Small and tight-fitting
Cheap and colourful
Old-fashioned and formal
questions.why: She says it's about 'wearing these oversized clothes that are overpriced'.

questions.q: What is the secret to the scumbro look?
options: Buying everything from charity shops
Making sure your clothes are clean
Wearing your parents' old clothes from the 1970s and 1980s
Looking like you made no effort, while showing you did
questions.why: Catherine says the trick is to look like you've made no effort but at the same time show you have.

questions.q: What irony does Catherine point out?
options: Charity shops are selling designer brands
Celebrities are buying cheap clothes
People pay a lot to look poor, and charities get nothing
Fashion victims give all their clothes to charity
questions.why: She says some pay lots to look like they wear second-hand clothes, but charity shops make no money from it.
